speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a breast mass. To begin my evaluation, please tell me your age and how long you have noticed this lump.

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given the rapid increase in size over four weeks, have you experienced any fever, skin changes like redness or dimpling, or pain in the area? Also, please tell me if you are currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor. The rapid growth of a painless breast mass in a 48-year-old woman without skin changes is highly characteristic of a benign or malignant phyllodes tumor rather than a carcinoma or abscess.
